title: Marguerite and the Songbook
premise: Theo Okonkwo, a wedding planner who no longer believes in marriage, is hired to stage a festival wedding at a decaying coastal estate — and finds a letter, postmarked eleven years ago and never delivered, hidden in the estate's old songbook. The letter was written by Marguerite, the estate's late owner, to the daughter she gave up; Theo tracks her down and discovers she is Ada, the estate's new heir, who has arrived intending to sell everything. As Theo plans a wedding he doesn't believe in for strangers while helping Ada confront an inheritance of secrets, the two fall into something neither planned. When the festival's last night arrives and Ada must choose between selling and staying, Theo finally lets someone stay after the last train leaves — and admits his own heart was never containable after all.
about_author: Emrys Blackwood is the pen name of a former estate archivist who spent years cataloguing other people's letters before writing any of their own. They live in a converted coach house on the coast, where they collect unsent mail and insist that every good love story begins with a delay.

chapters.title: The Muscle Theory
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He runs a flawless wedding for clients who cry through their vows, then goes home alone and rehearses his theory: the heart is trainable, containable. A call comes offering a lucrative festival wedding at Hollowmere Estate. Beat: competence as armor.

chapters.title: Hollowmere
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He tours the crumbling estate with its eccentric caretaker, Mrs. Vane, and learns the owner died months ago, leaving an estranged heir nobody can locate. The house feels like a held breath. Beat: unease beneath professional calm.

chapters.title: Ada Arrives
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She inherits Hollowmere from a mother she never knew existed until the lawyers called, and arrives intending to sign it over to developers by month's end. She meets Theo and mistakes him for staff. Beat: grief disguised as efficiency.

chapters.title: The Songbook
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. While measuring the music room for the ceremony, a shelf gives way and an old songbook spills open — inside it, a sealed letter postmarked eleven years ago, addressed in Marguerite's hand to 'my daughter.' Beat: the past intrudes on the present.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Theo shows Ada the letter; she refuses to read it, calling it a stranger's business. They negotiate: he gets the estate for the festival if he leaves the letter alone. Both are lying about what they want. Beat: friction that sparks.

chapters.title: What the Letter Says
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, alone at night. She reads it: Marguerite gave her up at birth, watched her from afar, and begged for one meeting Ada never knew was offered. The meeting date passed years ago. Beat: devastation, and anger at everyone who kept the secret.

chapters.title: Vendor Lists and Ghosts
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Wedding planning proceeds against a backdrop of Ada tearing through Marguerite's papers, hunting why the letter was never sent. Mrs. Vane knows more than she says. Theo recognizes avoidance when he sees it — his own specialty. Beat: reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: The Festival Contract
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The developers press her to close early; the festival contract would delay the sale. She signs it anyway, telling herself it's about money. Theo catches her crying in the orangery and pretends he didn't. Beat: the first crack in her resolve.

chapters.title: Train Schedules
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A quiet evening inventorying chairs becomes an argument about whether love is a decision or a weather event. Ada learns Theo hasn't been on a date in six years. He deflects; she notices. Beat: intimacy through sparring.

chapters.title: Mrs. Vane's Confession
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The caretaker admits Marguerite asked her to post the letter decades of times and she never did — protecting Marguerite's shame, or her own jealousy. Ada's fury finds a target. Beat: justice begins to look personal.

chapters.title: Rehearsal Dinner
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The rehearsal dinner he stages is beautiful and hollow, and watching the bride's father give a toast, Theo feels his containment theory fail publicly. Ada sees it happen. Beat: the planner starts believing despite himself.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Room
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She finally opens her mother's locked bedroom and finds photographs of herself at every age — school plays, graduations — taken from a distance. Marguerite never stopped watching. Beat: love discovered too late to answer.

chapters.title: The Storm
chapters.summary: Dual POV. A storm strands the wedding party; power fails; Theo and Ada shelter in the music room and trade truths — his broken engagement, her adoption files she's never opened. They almost kiss. Beat: rising heat, interrupted.

chapters.title: Sold to the Highest Bidder
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Cornered by the developers' final offer and terrified of staying anywhere, Ada accepts. She tells Theo the sale closes after the festival. He calls her a coward; she calls him a man who plans other people's courage. Beat: rupture.

chapters.title: The Missing Page
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Rereading the songbook for the ceremony music, he finds a second letter tucked in the binding — Marguerite's final entry, written weeks before her death, naming where she buried something 'for my daughter.' Beat: hope re-armed.

chapters.title: Digging
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Under the pear tree they unearth a tin: Marguerite's diary, adoption records, and an unposted reply — proof Ada once wrote back at nineteen, a letter Marguerite received and treasured but never answered out of fear. Beat: inheritance redefined.

chapters.title: The Wedding Day
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The festival wedding unfolds flawlessly, and Theo watches two strangers choose each other with total exposure and realizes what he's been refusing. During the vows, he looks for Ada and finds the lawn empty. Beat: climax of realization.

chapters.title: Last Train
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She's packed, keys on the table, the sale signed. At the platform she reads Marguerite's diary passage about choosing fear twice and misses the train on purpose — or lets it go without her. Beat: the choice made.

chapters.title: After the Last Train Leaves
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He finds Ada walking the dark road back, and instead of arguing, he simply walks beside her. He tells her the truth about his engagement: he left before he could be left. For once, he stays put. Beat: confession without conditions.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She voids the sale using the diary as evidence the estate was meant as Marguerite's apology-in-waiting, and converts Hollowmere into an archive for found letters. Mrs. Vane, forgiven but not forgotten, keeps the grounds. Beat: justice outside the law.

chapters.title: The Songbook, Continued
chapters.summary: Dual POV. On the festival's final night, the town gathers in the music room; Ada adds the first new page to the songbook — her letter to Marguerite, finally answered across time. Theo watches her and understands the heart was never a muscle to train. Beat: tenderness earned.

chapters.title: Staying
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, epilogue. One year later: Theo still plans weddings, now believing in them; Ada runs the archive; a new lost letter arrives weekly. On the porch after the season's last festival, neither checks the train schedule. Beat: quiet, chosen permanence.
